## Changed

- `structured` markdown reads tables from the page's drawing. A browser-printed
  HTML table or a typeset use table is the grid its rules draw; every character
  is placed in the cell its centre falls in, merged cells are read from missing
  rules and their value is written in every row and column they cover, and a
  header block repeated with other column widths becomes its own table. A
  table ruled between its rows only takes its columns from where its text
  starts, so two such lists side by side are two tables. Rows of filled chips
  with no rules are a table too, and when a table's cells carry two or more
  colours each value is followed by its colour's name (`R-1 [green]`). A
  framed text box, or a filled panel holding a paragraph, is its own block.
  Only `markdown` changes: `spans` and the `complex_table` routing flag are
  computed exactly as in 0.17.
- A table continued on the next page keeps the values the page break cut: a
  merged cell's value is written into the blank cells that continue it, and a
  value cut mid-sentence is written whole. A note printed across a table is
  written as paragraphs between two parts of it, each under the header.
- `structured` markdown keeps list markers as printed (`1.`, `a.`, `(2)`, `iv.`)
  and indents nested items, instead of replacing every marker with `- `. In an
  ordinance the marker is the provision's address.
- `structured` markdown reads page columns that share baselines, and a heading
  printed to the left of the text it heads, as columns; lines of sentences that
  happen to line up are no longer taken for a table.
- `structured` markdown table headers name each column in full (`Maximum
  Height - Stories`), and a table whose first row is data gets an empty header
  row instead of having that row taken for the column names. Table cells are
  escaped like the rest of the markdown and keep bold that sets part of a cell
  apart (`**Height:** 45 ft`).
- `structured` markdown ends a paragraph where a sentence ends well short of
  the column's edge, so notes and definitions printed one per line stay
  apart, and reads note markers printed tight against their note.
- A hyphen that ends a line is kept in `structured` markdown (`cul-de-sac`
  instead of `cul de-sac`).
- Text outside the page box is left out of `structured` markdown.

Measured on `data/text` (14 pages of zoning codes and plans from five cities,
six of them held out while the rules were written, and the 17 pages of the Los
Angeles Generalized Summary of Zoning Regulations, whose tables merge cells
across rows, columns and page breaks), each graded against a ledger of what
the page prints — cell values, that each table's first row names its columns,
passages, and notes that must stand apart: 1158 of 1158 checks, against 226
for 0.17, 373 for `pdftotext -layout` and 828 for the Docling server. On the
Los Angeles summary alone: 738 of 738, against 125, 31 and 504. The per-page table is produced by
`scripts/text-bench.py`; `tests/text_ledgers.rs` keeps the toolkit at full
marks.
